decisions.reason: The source specifies the power-routing relationship among three existing boards but does not change the four-board inventory or separate-board architecture owned by this Requirement.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records the INA219 position and combined downstream 3.3V measurement coverage.
The interboard power-routing clarification does not change connector accessibility, placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source does not alter the power board's dimensions, installation orientation, USB-C placement, aspect ratio, or mounting requirements.
The board power chain and INA219 placement do not change the charge-status display or dedicated charge-LED interface.
The existing state already covers the complete downstream 3.3V rail and Schottky source selection; the source does not change standalone USB supply behavior.
The source concerns power distribution and current measurement, not I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, cable length, or signal topology.
The source does not change the LED supply voltage, level shifting, GPIO assignment, or standby power control.
The interboard power path does not change the panel-control connector inventory, signal assignments, or on-board button policy.
The source discusses power connectors and 3.3V current flow, not USB data routing, enumeration, connector sourcing, or programming behavior.
Receiving forwarded power does not change the sensor board's independently stated role as a connector fanout for external sensors.
The current state already identifies DCDC1 as the primary 3.3V source for the main board and downstream sensors; the source adds routing and metering details without changing regulation requirements.
